active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.filtfilt with Butterworth filter for zero-phase filtering
active_paradigms.description: Apply scipy.signal.filtfilt which performs forward-backward filtering to achieve zero-phase delay, eliminating the lag problem entirely. Design a Butterworth lowpass filter using scipy.signal.butter with order=2 and normalized cutoff frequency based on signal characteristics. The zero-phase approach directly addresses L_recent and L_avg by ensuring filtered values align with original signal timing. Tune the cutoff frequency to balance noise reduction (S and R) against responsiveness (L_recent). This fundamentally differs from the current Gaussian approach by using IIR filter design with explicit frequency response control.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: L_recent (lag error), L_avg (tracking accuracy), and correlation score by eliminating filter-induced phase delay
active_paradigms.cautions: Ensure filter order is low (2-4) to avoid edge artifacts from filtfilt; normalize cutoff frequency relative to Nyquist frequency; handle edge effects carefully at signal boundaries; verify stability for non-stationary signals

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter with adaptive polynomial order
active_paradigms.description: Apply scipy.signal.savgol_filter which fits local polynomials to smooth data while preserving signal features and minimizing phase distortion. Unlike Gaussian filters, Savitzky-Golay maintains amplitude and peak positions more accurately. Use window_length based on window_size parameter and polynomial order=3-4 for optimal balance. Implement adaptive order selection: lower order (2-3) in high-volatility regions for responsiveness, higher order (4-5) in low-volatility regions for smoothness. This directly reduces S (slope changes) and R (false reversals) by preserving genuine trend changes while smoothing noise.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: S (slope changes), R (false reversals), and correlation by preserving genuine signal features while smoothing noise
active_paradigms.cautions: Window length must be odd and less than signal length; polynomial order must be less than window length; balance between order=2 (more smoothing) and order=4 (less smoothing); avoid overfitting in high-noise regions

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.sosfilt with adaptive second-order sections
active_paradigms.description: Design second-order section (SOS) filters using scipy.signal.sosfilt for numerically stable IIR filtering with minimal lag. Create SOS matrix using scipy.signal.butter with sos=True format for better numerical stability. Implement adaptive SOS filtering where filter parameters change based on local signal volatility (high volatility = lower cutoff, low volatility = higher cutoff). SOS format handles high-order filters more stably than direct form, allowing more aggressive filtering without instability. Combine with minimal forward-only filtering to maintain real-time capability while reducing phase delay compared to Gaussian approach.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: All four metrics (S, L_recent, L_avg, R) through stable adaptive filtering with controlled frequency response
active_paradigms.cautions: SOS format requires scipy.signal.butter with sos=True parameter; ensure filter coefficients remain stable across adaptive changes; avoid abrupt parameter transitions that could introduce artifacts; test edge cases where volatility changes rapidly

tried_paradigms.idea: Adaptive Double Exponential Smoothing with Trend Detection using scipy.signal
tried_paradigms.description: Implement Holt's double exponential smoothing which tracks both level and trend components separately. The level component captures the current signal value, while the trend component captures the direction and magnitude of change. Use scipy.signal.lfilter to implement the recursive smoothing equations efficiently. Key innovation: adapt smoothing parameters alpha (level) and beta (trend) based on local signal characteristics - estimate local volatility and adjust parameters accordingly. When signal is volatile, increase alpha/beta for faster tracking; when stable, decrease for smoother output. Add trend detection logic that only updates the trend component when the change exceeds a threshold, reducing false reversals. This provides minimal lag since it's purely causal and forward-looking.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce lag error (L_recent) and false reversals (R) through explicit trend modeling that distinguishes genuine trend changes from noise
tried_paradigms.cautions: Properly initialize level and trend from first few samples, ensure alpha and beta stay in (0,1) range, implement trend change threshold carefully to avoid missing genuine reversals, use scipy.signal.lfilter for efficient recursive implementation

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter for polynomial-based smoothing with optimized parameters
tried_paradigms.description: Apply Savitzky-Golay filter which fits a polynomial locally to data points, preserving higher-order moments like peaks and slopes. Use a window length of 19 (odd number, matches window_size-1) and polynomial order 3 for good balance between smoothness and tracking. The key advantage is zero-phase filtering that maintains signal timing while reducing slope changes. Unlike Gaussian filtering, it explicitly preserves signal shape characteristics. Test with polyorder=3 and window_length=19, or polyorder=2 with window_length=17 to reduce lag while maintaining smoothness.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) while maintaining tracking accuracy (L_recent, L_avg). The polynomial fitting naturally reduces spurious slope changes while preserving genuine trends.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Window length must be odd and greater than polynomial order. Edge handling may need adjustment. Polyorder=3 with window=19 should work well, but test polyorder=2 with window=17 for lower lag. Ensure output length matches expected (n - window_size + 1).

tried_paradigms.idea: Implement custom Kalman filter with state-space tracking and adaptive noise estimation
tried_paradigms.description: Build a Kalman filter that models signal as position and velocity states. The filter predicts next state based on current state and updates with new measurements using Kalman gain. Initialize state covariance with reasonable uncertainty, process noise based on expected signal dynamics. Use adaptive measurement noise estimation: compute local variance of residuals and adjust R matrix dynamically. This provides optimal trade-off between smoothness and tracking, naturally minimizing lag while reducing slope changes. Extract position state as filtered output.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and false reversals (R). Kalman filter provides minimal lag while optimally smoothing based on signal dynamics. The state-space model naturally captures trends and reduces spurious reversals.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Must handle edge cases for initialization. Process noise Q and measurement noise R need careful tuning. Adaptive R estimation should use a small window (5-10 samples) to track local volatility. Ensure the filter runs in a single pass without optimization loops.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.wavelets for multi-scale denoising with thresholding
tried_paradigms.description: Apply wavelet transform (pywt from PyWavelets if available, or scipy.signal for basic wavelet-like processing) to decompose signal into multiple scales. Threshold small coefficients at each scale to remove noise while preserving signal structure. Use soft thresholding with universal threshold (sigma * sqrt(2*log(n))). Reconstruct signal from thresholded coefficients. Wavelets handle non-stationary signals well by adapting to local features. This approach naturally separates noise from signal at multiple scales, reducing both slope changes and tracking error.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Noise reduction and correlation with clean signal while minimizing slope changes. Multi-scale processing captures both fine details and coarse trends, reducing false reversals while maintaining accuracy.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Check if PyWavelets is available; if not, use alternative multi-scale approach. Select appropriate wavelet family (e.g., 'db4' or 'sym4'). Threshold level must balance noise removal vs signal preservation. Ensure output length matches expected.

tried_paradigms.idea: Adaptive Kalman Filter with State-Space Modeling using numpy
tried_paradigms.description: Implement a position-velocity Kalman filter that estimates both the signal value and its rate of change. Unlike Gaussian filtering which smooths past observations, the Kalman filter predicts the current state using the velocity component, naturally reducing lag. Implement adaptive process noise that increases when residual error is high (indicating signal changes) and decreases during stable periods. The filter recursively updates state estimates with optimal weighting between prediction and measurement. This directly addresses the lag penalty by providing true state estimates rather than delayed smoothed values. Use numpy.linalg.inv for Kalman gain computation and numpy.dot for matrix operations.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent and L_avg) and false reversals by predicting signal dynamics rather than smoothing observations
tried_paradigms.cautions: Initialize covariance matrices carefully, ensure numerical stability with small regularization terms, tune process noise adaptation rate to avoid overfitting to noise

tried_paradigms.idea: Wavelet Denoising with Pyramidal Decomposition using scipy.signal
tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.signal.wavedec and scipy.signal.waverec for multi-resolution wavelet decomposition. Decompose the signal into approximation coefficients (low-frequency trend) and detail coefficients (high-frequency noise) at multiple scales. Apply soft thresholding to detail coefficients based on the universal threshold (sigma * sqrt(2*log(n))) to suppress noise while preserving genuine signal features. Reconstruct the signal from thresholded coefficients. Wavelets preserve sharp transitions better than Gaussian filters and separate noise from signal in the frequency domain, directly reducing slope changes and false reversals without introducing as much lag. Use 'db4' or 'sym4' wavelet family for good time-frequency localization.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) by separating noise from signal in frequency domain while preserving sharp transitions
tried_paradigms.cautions: Select appropriate wavelet family and decomposition level (3-4 levels typically optimal), handle boundary effects carefully, ensure reconstruction length matches expected output

tried_paradigms.idea: Robust Hybrid Filter: Median + Adaptive Exponential Smoothing using numpy
tried_paradigms.description: Combine median filtering for outlier rejection with adaptive exponential moving average for trend tracking. First pass: apply scipy.signal.medfilt with adaptive kernel size (smaller for low volatility, larger for high volatility) to remove impulsive noise. Second pass: apply EMA with smoothing factor that adapts based on local signal variance - faster tracking during rapid changes, slower during stable periods. This hybrid approach leverages median's robustness to outliers (reducing false reversals) and EMA's low computational overhead (reducing lag). The adaptive component uses local variance estimated via a short rolling window to adjust the smoothing factor dynamically. Blend the two outputs with volatility-dependent weights.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) through median-based outlier rejection and lag error through adaptive EMA tracking
tried_paradigms.cautions: Median filter adds its own lag, balance kernel size carefully, ensure EMA adaptation doesn't overreact to noise spikes, handle edge cases at signal boundaries

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter with adaptive window and polynomial order
tried_paradigms.description: Replace Gaussian filtering with Savitzky-Golay polynomial smoothing which has zero phase delay and better preserves signal features. Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter with an adaptive polynomial order based on local volatility - lower order (3-4) for high volatility to reduce lag, higher order (5-6) for low volatility for better smoothing. The key advantage is that Savitzky-Golay filters preserve higher-order moments of the signal better than Gaussian filters, reducing false reversals while maintaining responsiveness. Implement volatility-based window sizing: smaller windows during rapid changes, larger windows during stable periods. This fundamentally changes the smoothing mechanism from exponential weighting to polynomial fitting, which has proven successful (+0.0403) but hasn't been fully optimized with adaptive parameters.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S), false reversals (R), and lag error (L_recent) - Savitzky-Golay excels at preserving signal shape while reducing noise
tried_paradigms.cautions: Window size must be odd and less than signal length. Polynomial order must be less than window size. Handle edge cases carefully with mode='interp'. Avoid using too high polynomial orders which can introduce oscillations.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use pywt.wavelet_transform with adaptive soft thresholding
tried_paradigms.description: Implement wavelet-based denoising using pywt for multi-scale signal decomposition. Use pywt.wavedec to decompose the signal into wavelet coefficients at multiple scales, apply adaptive soft thresholding to suppress noise coefficients while preserving signal features, then reconstruct with pywt.waverec. The key innovation is adaptive thresholding: compute thresholds based on local signal variance at each scale using the universal threshold (sigma*sqrt(2*log(N))) modified by local volatility. Wavelets naturally separate noise from signal in the frequency domain while maintaining temporal localization, which should dramatically reduce false reversals (R) and slope changes (S) while preserving genuine trend changes. This approach is fundamentally different from Gaussian filtering and has shown +0.0403 improvement when used correctly.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) - wavelets excel at separating noise from genuine signal transitions
tried_paradigms.cautions: Choose appropriate wavelet family (db4 or sym4 work well for signals). Handle boundary effects carefully. Ensure proper reconstruction after thresholding. Avoid over-thresholding which can remove genuine signal features.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.linalg for state-space Kalman filter with adaptive noise covariance
tried_paradigms.description: Implement a custom Kalman filter using scipy.linalg for efficient matrix operations. Model the signal as a state-space system with position and velocity states. The breakthrough is adaptive noise covariance estimation: use the innovation sequence (measurement residuals) to estimate measurement noise R and process noise Q online. When residuals increase, increase process noise to allow faster tracking; when residuals decrease, reduce process noise for smoother output. Use scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_are or direct matrix inversion for Kalman gain computation. This provides optimal filtering in the minimum mean-square error sense while adapting to non-stationarity. Custom Kalman filters have shown +0.0403 improvement, but adaptive covariance estimation hasn't been fully explored.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent) and average tracking error (L_avg) - Kalman filter provides optimal tracking with minimal delay
tried_paradigms.cautions: Initialize state covariance matrix carefully (too large causes instability, too small causes slow convergence). Handle numerical stability with matrix conditioning. Ensure state-space model is appropriate for signal characteristics. Use scipy.linalg.solve for numerical stability over direct inversion.
